visual_source_files.evidence: GitHub tree/README identify this as the test_discoformer.py 2D score-field output; PNG metadata reports 1800×750 RGB RGBA at 150 dpi. It is not identical to the paper Figure 3 and no exact figure-generation script is present.

source_acquisition.search_note: PDF首页、正文、参考文献未给出代码仓库；reading提供 arXiv:2511.05924 与 OpenReview forum gyOWJpP8cQ，无 supplementary。reports/tables/visual_source_inventory.csv 的目标行仍为 no_public_source_found，visual_source_files_local.csv 无目标行，corpus/visual_sources/icml-2026-cb506acd46ca/ 不存在。agent-reach doctor --json 将 GitHub 标为 warn（gh CLI/显式认证配置但未自动执行认证写操作）；unicli scholar code 对完整标题通过 github-scholar 返回同一仓库，match_type=title_exact、relationship=candidate-implementation、confidence=0.98 且 is_official_code=false；gh完整标题搜索随后找到公开未归档仓库 https://github.com/celerychen/discoformer，其README直接链接该论文题目和 arXiv:2511.05924v2。gh API树核对 README、discoformer.py、test_discoformer.py、score_comparison_2d.png 和权重/PDF；未读取或克隆权重、数据集、checkpoint。仓库没有 plot*/figure*/visual*/table*脚本、notebook、TeX/TikZ/PGF或样式文件，只有一个由测试脚本生成的150 dpi PNG，故记为 partial_visual_source，不能把论文PDF的视觉参数标为 source_exact。

paper_style.palette_strategy: 正文图像以 viridis 类连续色标表达 attention/density 强度，Matplotlib 蓝/橙/红/绿/紫/青区分 estimator、score role 和 TTT budget；表格保持黑色数字与横线，最佳值多用粗体。
paper_style.vector_raster_mix: Letter 双栏正文、caption、表格横线和文字主要是 PDF vector；Figure 1/3–11、12–15 的图面以 RGB 栅格嵌入，代码框和图框/文字为 vector，整体 mixed。
paper_style.style_consistency: Nimbus Roman/Times-like serif 与 Computer Modern math 在正文、caption、表格和公式中稳定；图内 axes/legend 使用 Matplotlib 风格 sans-serif，Figure 2 使用 Nimbus Mono 等宽体。booktabs/minimal 表格一致，但图的颜色、legend 密度与独立 heatmap normalization 造成局部可读性差异。

figures.label: Figure 1

caption.text: Figure 1. Attention visualization. Top: average attention in layer 0 from query x; heatmaps show the attention matrix and the normalized KDE matrix Dᵢⱼ ∝ e^(−∥xᵢ−xⱼ∥²/2), and scatter plots show very high agreement. Bottom: individual heads exhibit emergent specialization (close-range, far-range, directional).

color.semantic_mapping: viridis encodes attention score/heatmap intensity; red, blue and green encode true, predicted and KDE score vectors; black/red crosses mark means and chosen point.

plot_grammar.legend_placement: lower-left for top field; per-panel head titles/colorbars

encodings.x: 2D sample/query coordinates in the score field; query/key indices in the two matrices
encodings.y: 2D sample/query coordinates; query index in the matrices
encodings.shape: arrows, points, black means and red chosen-point cross
encodings.facet: top field, two matrices, two correlations, four selected heads
encodings.text: Score comparison title, correlation values, head titles and legends

figures.data_and_statistics: n=1000 GMM sample for the spatial field. The two heatmaps compare layer-0 average attention with a normalized KDE matrix; correlation panels show corr=0.930 and corr=0.841; the top legend reports Transformer MSE=0.0366. No uncertainty or repeated-trial dispersion is shown.
figures.evidence_relation: Proposition 3.3–3.6 claim that attention recovers/reweights Gaussian KDE → this mechanism composite; Figure 2 supplies the whitening/core interface and Table 1 checks its equivariance; Appendix Figures 12–13 expand all heads and query-conditioned behavior.
design_strengths: Combines field, matrix, correlation and head behavior in one mechanism chain.
MSE/correlation, means and chosen point bind the qualitative attention story to observed data.
The head grid exposes a concrete multi-scale kernel interpretation.
design_weaknesses: Nine panels and small colorbars make the right-column composite dense at print size.
Heatmap scales and head axis/parameter labels are hard to compare without enlarging.
Color carries several semantic roles with little shape/line-style redundancy.
figures.reusable_pattern: Use a top-to-bottom composite of field → attention/KDE matrix → agreement statistic → individual-head specialization; in a reusable version share color normalization and add panel labels/explicit query conditions.

evidence.label: Rendered Figure 1 composite: score field, two matrices, two correlation scatters and four head scatters

figures.label: Figure 3

caption.text: Figure 3. Score estimation comparison between Scott KDE (Scott, 2015) and our transformer model. The transformer is more accurate, especially in the sparse regions. We plot the negated score for easier viewing.

color.semantic_mapping: Red, blue and green arrow fields denote true, Transformer and KDE scores; gray/black points provide sample/mean context.

encodings.line: negated score vector direction and length
encodings.text: Score comparison n=1000 title and MSE values in the legend

figures.data_and_statistics: A 2D unimodal Gaussian with n=1000. The legend reports Transformer MSE=0.0077 and KDE MSE=0.1528; there are no uncertainty marks or repeated-trial summaries.
figures.evidence_relation: First direct result for the abstract accuracy claim: Figure 1 explains the learned attention/KDE mechanism, Figure 4 and Table 2 extend this point to dimension/sample-size scaling, and Appendix Figure 15 checks the cost boundary.
design_strengths: Spatial arrows make sparse-region behavior visually concrete.
True, Transformer and KDE are co-located on identical coordinates and summarized with MSE.
design_weaknesses: Dense arrows overlap, making per-point method attribution difficult.
MSE appears only in the legend and sparse regions are not explicitly bounded.
No uncertainty or repeated evaluation is shown.

caption.text: Figure 4. Left: MSE of score estimation in dimensions 1 and 10 on a 3-modal GMM using Transformer and KDE. The Transformer has excellent scaling in both dimension d and the sample size n. Right: MSE of score estimation using the Transformer on GMMs with different numbers of modes. Despite being trained only on GMMs with 1-10 modes, and n = 2048, the model exhibits excellent generalization.

Training/test support and error aggregation are carried mostly by caption/body text.
Claims of excellent scaling are not accompanied by uncertainty.

figures.label: Figure 11

caption.text: Figure 11. Comparison between the trained Transformer model and Scott KDE on the task of numerically solving the homogeneous Landau equation. We plot the first entry of the covariance matrix Σ₁,₁(t) of the numerical solutions and ground truth, when known. The left two panels use Maxwell collisions, while the last panel shows Coulomb collisions. The Transformer outperforms KDE, and is comparable in quality to SBTM in (Ilin et al., 2025).

color.semantic_mapping: Blue/orange distinguish KDE/Transformer; black dashed curve is analytic/equilibrium reference.

encodings.line: solid numerical trajectories and dashed analytic/equilibrium curve

figures.data_and_statistics: Three time trajectories at n=500 for Maxwell (d=3,d=10) and Coulomb (d=3); analytic/equilibrium ground truth is shown when known. No ensemble interval, solver-step uncertainty or repeated run summary.
figures.evidence_relation: Section 4.7 connects the pre-trained score oracle to a Landau/Fokker–Planck particle solver without simulation-time retraining; Figure 15 supplies the runtime/memory boundary and Figures 6/10 the other plug-in uses.
design_strengths: Same observable and reference style across physical regimes.
Dashed reference gives some non-color redundancy.
design_weaknesses: No SBTM trajectory is plotted despite the caption comparison.
Solver discretization, time step and variation are absent.
Panel ranges are not fully identical, limiting direct amplitude comparison.
figures.reusable_pattern: Show one observable across physical regimes with reference curves and explicitly mark which regimes have ground truth; pair with a solver-error/cost table.

figures.label: Figure 12

caption.text: Figure 12. We visualize attention of the eight individual heads of layer 0 as a heatmap. Yellow color denotes higher attention weight and blue is lower. We choose the particle ordering so that nearby particles are close in the ordering. Heads 0, 2, and 5 specialize on nearby points, heads 1 and 6 specialize on far-away points, whereas heads 3, 4, and 7 attend in specific directions.

design_strengths: Covers all eight heads under one particle ordering.

design_weaknesses: Per-head colorbars make absolute cross-head intensity comparisons ambiguous.
Index axes are not physical coordinates, so direction interpretation depends on the accompanying text.

figures.label: Figure 15

caption.text: Figure 15. Runtime comparison between KDE and the Transformer model in 2 and 10 dimensions. Both are O(n²) asymptotically, but empirically the Transformer scales better and has improved memory efficiency. KDE encounters an OOM error at n = 2¹⁵.

figures.evidence_relation: Table 2’s large-n OOM and score accuracy → runtime/memory cost boundary; Appendix E explains the practical attention-kernel versus naive-KDE difference, while Figure 14 shows retraining as another cost.
design_strengths: Log-log axes show crossover and empirical scaling in both dimensions.
OOM is visible as a failure boundary rather than silently omitted.
Dashed fits provide trend information beyond raw points.

Censored KDE series makes slope comparison sensitive to the stopping point.
Caption omits the small-n KDE advantage/crossover described in the body.
figures.reusable_pattern: Combine dimension facets, wall-clock curves, empirical slope fits and explicit OOM censoring; report hardware and repeated timing statistics alongside it.

caption.text: Table 5. Score and log-density estimation in d = 100 on random 2-component diagonal-covariance GMMs (n = 2048 context, 256 queries). KDE baselines use two bandwidth strategies; “Oracle h” is the best fixed bandwidth found by grid search. DiScoFormer (d_model = 256, 8 heads, 6 layers) is evaluated at 150k training steps.

tables.data_and_statistics: Rows Scott KDE, Oracle h KDE and DiScoFormer; columns Score MSE and Log-density MSE. Values: 1.155/967, 1.090/781 and 0.167/20.8; DiScoFormer is bold. Score precision is three decimals while log-density mixes integer and one decimal.
tables.evidence_relation: High-dimensional extension of Figure 4/Table 2; Oracle h prevents an uncompetitive fixed-bandwidth baseline and Figure 15 supplies the practical cost boundary.
design_strengths: Places both outputs and a strong KDE bandwidth baseline together.
Caption gives d, context/query sizes, model configuration and training budget.
design_weaknesses: Mixed precision across log-density cells.
No seed/aggregation and bold rule not stated.
The high-dimensional result is a single table without uncertainty.
tables.reusable_pattern: In a high-dimensional comparison, put multiple output metrics and an oracle baseline in one table, with the evaluation budget fully stated.

caption.text: Table 6. Ablation: effect of whitening on score and density estimation (d = 1). ID and OOD use different log-uniform meta-distributions over GMM location and scale parameters; OOD scales are well beyond the training range.

tables.uncertainty: No uncertainty; ID/OOD and whitening values are single point MSEs.

tables.evidence_relation: Directly tests Figure 2 whitening/Proposition 3.1 motivation; contrasts structural normalization with Figure 5’s test-time adaptation and supports the rotation/scale boundary in Limitations.
design_strengths: Paired ID/OOD groups expose catastrophic OOD failure clearly.
Score and density outputs are evaluated together.
design_weaknesses: Exact ID/OOD parameter ranges and bold rule are omitted.
Group label and metric header hierarchy are compact enough to require careful reading.
tables.reusable_pattern: Use paired ID/OOD row groups to isolate a structural component and report both primary outputs; state ranges and aggregation explicitly.

cross_object_system.visual_narrative: Figure 2/Table 1 establish whitening and equivariance; Figure 1 links attention to KDE; Figure 3–5 and Tables 2–4 quantify score accuracy, scaling and TTT; Tables 5–6 add high-dimensional and whitening boundaries; Figure 6–11 show Fisher, SD-KDE, entropy and Landau plug-in uses; Figures 12–15 complete head specialization, score-matching failure and runtime/OOM evidence.
cross_object_system.caption_system: Captions use italic Figure/Table label followed by a descriptive sentence or comparison statement. Most captions provide title plus setup/comparison, while Figure 1/4/7/10/11/15 also state a main finding; uncertainty definitions, replicate counts and bold/highlight rules are usually absent.
cross_object_system.table_header_system: Tables use short serif headers, n or Method as the first column, and grouped dimension/method headers only where needed (Table 2). Metrics are MSE/relative MSE with occasional mixed decimal precision; ID/OOD appears as a row group in Table 6.
cross_object_system.method_result_ablation_link: Figure 2 and Table 1 ground the whitening/equivariance interface; Figure 1 and Appendix Figures 12–13 ground attention–KDE mechanism; score/density results and TTT appear in Figures 3–10/Tables 2–5; Table 6 isolates whitening under ID/OOD, separating structural normalization from TTT.
cross_object_system.main_appendix_link: Main Figure 1 selected four heads, expanded by all-head matrix/scatter views in Figures 12–13; main no-retraining score claim is stress-tested by Figure 14, and Table 2/score results receive runtime/memory boundary evidence in Figure 15. Appendix captions and text make the layer/head and failure conditions explicit but not always in the main captions.
cross_object_system.typography_consistency: The paper’s serif/Computer Modern typography and minimal table rules are stable across main and appendix. Matplotlib sans-serif labels become smaller in dense grids, particularly Figures 1, 10, 13 and 15.
cross_object_system.color_consistency: Viridis consistently maps attention/density magnitude, while blue/orange/red/green/purple identify methods or score roles. However, independent colorbars and color-only curve identities mean most objects are not robustly grayscale safe.

most_reusable_patterns: Figure 1’s field → matrix → correlation → head-specialization mechanism composite.
Figure 7/8’s truth-first qualitative comparison tied to panel/legend MISE.
Table 2/5/6’s grouped dimension/OOD/failure and ID/OOD ablation layouts.
Figure 15’s log-log runtime curves with empirical slopes and explicit OOM censoring.
highest_value_objects: Figure 4 + Table 2：score dimension/sample-size scaling and extrapolation。
Table 5 + Table 6：high-dimensional performance and whitening boundary。
failure_patterns: 颜色承担主要语义且多数图灰度不安全。
caption 常写 excellent/best/outperforms，却没有 seed、重复或 uncertainty 定义。
Figure 1/13 的高 panel 密度压缩 axis、legend 与 colorbar；heatmap 的独立 normalization 限制跨 panel 比较。
表格的粗体规则、MSE 分母和聚合方式不总在 caption 中说明；OOM/slope 的 censoring 语义需要更明确。
final_judgment.one_sentence_visual_strategy: 以白化与 attention–KDE 机制为入口，用 score/density 主比较、OOD/高维消融建立效果边界，再以 Fisher/entropy/PDE 插件和附录 attention、score-matching、runtime 图补齐机制、失败与成本证据。
